title: Grace Hopper's A-0 helped replace numeric instructions with words
body: In 1952 Grace Hopper completed A-0, a system that could assemble previously prepared routines into a program. It let the operator specify routines using a more human-readable notation than the computer's raw instructions.
takeaway: Reusing prepared pieces of code means each new program need not start from the machine's smallest operations.
source: Computer History Museum, Timeline of Computer History (1952)

title: A 1968 computer demo showed collaborators working at a distance
body: In December 1968 Douglas Engelbart and his team demonstrated their interactive system to a San Francisco audience. The presentation showed people in different locations using the computer together over a live link.
takeaway: Shared work on a screen was an idea researchers could demonstrate decades before home internet became common.
source: Computer History Museum, The Mother of All Demos (1968)
